builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Vulnerable Models in the AI Supply Chain: An Empirical Study of Adoption, Propagation, and Usage Patterns
summary: This is an empirical measurement study, not a new method; its actionable output replaces informal trust in model-hub artifacts with explicit provenance verification, dependency scanning against vulnerability databases such as InsightDB, and application-layer integration guardrails, since registry-level file scanning alone proved insufficient. The cost is modest engineering effort: adding dependency auditing to CI, pinning and verifying model sources, preferring safe serialization formats, and disabling permissive framework defaults, with negligible runtime overhead. Adoption can fail because the underlying vulnerability database is incomplete (only 22.1% of flagged models were found actively referenced, implying both false negatives in scanning and stale flags), so point-in-time checks may miss newly disclosed or propagated vulnerabilities in fine-tuning chains.
rationale: The study provides direct evidence that vulnerable models propagate unchecked into thousands of repositories with no sanitization or provenance checks, so a small team deploying third-party models should immediately adopt provenance verification and dependency scanning as low-cost, high-value hygiene.
technique: AI supply-chain vulnerability auditing and integration guardrails
